newsitem.title: UK: GDR REPORT - India recovers with Bombay rise.
newsitem.headline: GDR REPORT - India recovers with Bombay rise.

text.p: Indian global depositary receipts bounced back on Wednesday following a similar recovery in Bomaby earlier as traders remained hopeful that a current political crisis would not affect recent reforms.
The GDR market, closed for four days for the Easter break, fell over eight percent on Tuesday in line with a slide in the local market.
The fall followed news on Sunday that the Congress Party had withdrawn its support for Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda's coalition government.
Also, news on Wednesday that the BJP Party could lend a hand to Gowda in a confidence vote on April 11 helped sentiment.
Traders said a key factor in the recovery had been hopes that the investor friendly 1997/8 budget would be passed despite the political impasse.
Reliance managed a $1 gain to $16.25/$17.00, and SBI added 67 cents to $20.25/75. VSNL rose $1 to $17.15/50.
The HSBC James Capel Indian GDR index JCEAI closed three points, or 4.24 percent, up at 73.72 points, with the premium over the local market at 18.48 percent from 17.85 percent.
The Bombay Stock Exchange 30-share index added 111.38 points to 3,538.39.
The Capel Korea GDR Index ended 0.99 points, or 1.64 percent, up at 61.17, a premium of 26.01 percent over the local market.
The Capel Taiwan GDR Index ended up 0.56 points, or 0.46 percent, at 122.20, a discount of 5.17 percent.
